name: Madlib
hook: A California producer who made most of Madvillainy in a Brazilian hotel room on a small sampler, and who traded beats by post with J Dilla.

blurb.age7: A producer from California who makes beats from dusty old records. He made a famous album with MF DOOM.
blurb.age13: Otis Jackson Jr. grew up in Oxnard, California, the son of musicians. As Madlib he makes beats from obscure records: jazz, soul, Brazilian music, film soundtracks. He made most of the music for Madvillainy, his 2004 album with MF DOOM, on a trip to Brazil, in his hotel room, using a small Boss SP-303 sampler, a turntable and a tape deck. With J Dilla he made the album Champion Sound as Jaylib, each of them rapping over the other's beats in different cities.
blurb.adult: Madlib is the clearest example on the map of the producer as the author of a record, and of minimal gear making major records. Madvillainy's instrumentals came off a portable sampler in a hotel room. His collaborations with J Dilla (Jaylib, 2003) and MF DOOM (Madvillain, 2004), both on Stones Throw, link Detroit's rhythmic innovation to the West Coast's crate-digging.
